text.en: A tree stands for years with leaves, shade and fruit; how hard is it to remove it?

The poet explains that killing a tree is not easy. A simple jab of the knife does not do it. The tree has grown slowly, drinking in sun, air and soil, so it has to be hacked, pulled out by the roots, scorched and left to die slowly in the sun.
The poem is a quiet protest against cutting down trees. By describing how long a tree takes to grow and how much effort it takes to destroy it, the poet makes us respect nature. Only when the roots are exposed and the green fades does the tree finally die.
Notice the many verbs of violence: hack, chop, pull, scorch. Watch for the contrast between the slow growth and quick destruction, and the use of everyday words.
